policy: Compare passage-level contributions, not votes for a conclusion. Several records can depend on the same surviving textual channel. Compatibility, literary dependence, institutional continuity and personal identity are different claims.

claims.title: James receives and transmits knowledge
claims.contribution: Knowledge is reported as passing through named recipients and subsequent transmitters.
claims.boundary: The complete Hypotyposes is not independently recovered here, and the knowledge is not identified as Thomas.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare transmitted content and authority without equating knowledge with membership in a later Gnostic school.

claims.title: James is portrayed with priestly functions
claims.contribution: Linen, holy-place access and intercession make priestly representation a concrete comparison.
claims.boundary: The portrayal does not document a Zadokite or Oniad pedigree.
claims.nextQuestion: Test whether the portrait preserves an office, ritual authority, or retrospective authorization.

claims.title: Kinship in the reported succession
claims.contribution: Symeon is presented as succeeding James with a kinship rationale.
claims.boundary: The same account classifies Essenes as opponents; it is not an unqualified admission of institutional identity.
claims.nextQuestion: Keep family, office and partisan classifications distinct when testing continuity.

claims.title: The particular brother relationship
claims.contribution: Paul singles out James through a relationship to the Lord and recounts a visit after three years.
claims.boundary: Spiritual kinship elsewhere does not automatically explain this particular relationship; the three years do not measure the prior persecution.
claims.nextQuestion: Explain the relational wording under the earlier-founder and namesake-successor alternatives.

claims.title: Recognition and division of mission
claims.contribution: Paul reports recognition from James, Cephas and John and a division of mission.
claims.boundary: This is Paul's own presentation, not an independent record of every participant's intentions.
claims.nextQuestion: Ask how a rival mission could seek acknowledgment while maintaining a contested program.

claims.title: Shared meals and contested authority
claims.contribution: The meal conflict involves arrivals associated with James.
claims.boundary: The paragraph does not explicitly state that James personally ordered the withdrawal.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare association, command and retrospective self-defense rather than attributing an unwritten instruction.

claims.title: James in the Festus-Albinus interval
claims.contribution: The paragraph provides an administrative interval and identifies James through Jesus called Christ.
claims.boundary: Reading the passage is not a completed authenticity investigation or a license to transfer the death to another person.
claims.nextQuestion: Specify whether a challenge concerns wording, personal identity, succession or the larger biographical frame.

claims.title: Law, Creator and opposition to Paul
claims.contribution: The description combines law observance and opposition to Paul with Creator affirmation.
claims.boundary: A hostile external category is not a timeless self-description or automatically a creator-rejecting cosmology.
claims.nextQuestion: Identify which features could persist and which would require a demonstrable transformation.

claims.title: Differences inside an inherited label
claims.contribution: Eusebius distinguishes views among those labeled Ebionites and reports use of a Hebrews gospel.
claims.boundary: The reported gospel title is not automatically an identification of a surviving manuscript or Irenaeus's Matthew.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare the classifiers' access and purposes before combining their descriptions.

claims.title: James as the communal destination
claims.contribution: The disciples are directed toward James after Jesus's departure.
claims.boundary: The saying does not supply a calendar date or an explicit ritual of appointing a replacement Christ.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare communal authority with the different authority attributed to Thomas in the next saying.

claims.title: Thomas and the private exchange
claims.contribution: Thomas receives a private exchange and withholds its sayings from the others.
claims.boundary: The passage does not explicitly instruct recruitment of twelve strangers or repeated biographical reenactment.
claims.nextQuestion: State how the succession-through-teaching proposal extends beyond the surviving narrative.

claims.title: Interpretation changes the recipient
claims.contribution: Life through interpretation, self-knowledge and transformation motivate a formation-oriented reading.
claims.boundary: These translated passages are not measurements or ancient formulations of neural phase dynamics.
claims.nextQuestion: Distinguish repeated belief from an operative change in perception, motives and choice.

claims.title: Blocked access to knowledge in Thomas
claims.contribution: The saying criticizes authorities who prevent entry to knowledge.
claims.boundary: A shared criticism does not settle literary direction or the identity of a displaced priestly institution.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare the operation of gatekeeping with Luke and proposed historical carriers.

claims.title: Blocked access to knowledge in Luke
claims.contribution: A related accusation concerns experts who obstruct entry.
claims.boundary: The relationship to Thomas can have more than one explanation.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare shared tradition, dependence and separate adaptation before selecting a transmission route.

claims.title: Non-material brotherhood in a James revelation
claims.locator: First Apocalypse of James, opening exchange
claims.contribution: The opening explicitly distinguishes its brother language from material kinship.
claims.boundary: This is a different text and setting from Galatians; direct page retrieval was unavailable and the opening was consulted through indexed translation.
claims.nextQuestion: Test the meaning of each relational claim rather than moving a definition unchanged between genres.

claims.title: The actual coverage of partial Greek witnesses
claims.locator: Published extract, description of P.Oxy. 1 and P.Oxy. 655
claims.contribution: The extract specifies partial saying coverage rather than a complete Greek collection.
claims.boundary: The full article, line-41 proposal and manuscript images were not reviewed here.
claims.nextQuestion: Collate the witness containing each relevant saying before using a copy date for an entire collection.

claims.title: A copied James revelation and proposed educational use
claims.contribution: The researchers report fifth/sixth-century Greek fragments and infer educational use from syllabic divisions.
claims.boundary: This is a reported First Apocalypse of James witness, not Thomas or a genealogical record; image rights remain with the named owner.
claims.nextQuestion: Review the critical publication and competing explanations of the scribal format.

claims.title: An earlier James and visionary-reading comparison
claims.locator: The Gospel of Thomas and the Hermeneutics of Vision, 2002 essay
claims.contribution: Owens connects James, apocalyptic inheritance and transformation of the interpreter.
claims.boundary: The comparison is not a demonstrated genealogy or a documented influence on the older conversations.
claims.nextQuestion: Credit the preceding interpretation and distinguish the additional earlier-founder chronological claim.

claims.contribution: Seven weeks, 62 weeks and a final week require explicit event assignments.
claims.boundary: A numerical sequence alone does not identify its persons or choose a modern calendar anchor.
claims.nextQuestion: State the beginning event and which anointed figure belongs to each interval.
claims.title: Daniel 9:24-27

claims.locator: CD 1:3-11, as discussed in Collins section J
claims.contribution: 390 years followed by 20 precede the Teacher's appearance in the discussed chronology.
claims.boundary: A chosen 586 BCE anchor yields an illustrative 176 BCE appearance, not a date inscribed in the text.
claims.nextQuestion: Collate the Hebrew witness and evaluate independent anchoring evidence.
claims.title: CD 1:3-11, as discussed in Collins section J

claims.contribution: The reconstructed 40-year career completes 390 + 20 + 40 + 40 = 490.
claims.boundary: The career interval is supplied; it must not be labeled as directly attested like the other intervals.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare proposed career, office and generation interpretations before identifying a death.
claims.title: CD 20:15 and Collins section J

claims.locator: 11Q13 II 6-7 in Williams's translation and discussion
claims.contribution: Williams adopts a reading placing liberation at the beginning of the cycle after ten jubilees.
claims.boundary: The older tenth-jubilee reading remains a distinct restoration; neither fixes a Teacher identity or a BCE date.
claims.nextQuestion: Independently collate II 6-7 and II 18 against the critical edition and photographs.
claims.title: 11Q13 II 6-7 in Williams's translation and discussion

claims.contribution: 364-day and 365-day idealized units differ by 490 days across 490 years.
claims.boundary: This is not a model of practical intercalation and cannot alone shift a chronology by a century.
claims.nextQuestion: Distinguish calendar operation from the count's chosen historical starting event.
claims.title: Published abstract, DOI 10.31743/vv.1935

claims.contribution: The account supplies royal permission, priests and Levites, and a scriptural argument for a sanctuary in Egypt.
claims.boundary: Reported correspondence is not an independently inspected original royal document.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare the Greek text, the identity of the founder and competing foundation dates.
claims.title: Antiquities 13.3.1-3

claims.contribution: Chelcias and Ananias are identified as sons of the founder; Ananias defends Alexander against a proposed dispossession.
claims.boundary: This supplies candidate carriers and contact, not proof of Essene affiliation or Thomas transmission.
claims.nextQuestion: Trace the family and institutional relations in independently supported evidence.
claims.title: Antiquities 13.10.4 and 13.13.2

claims.contribution: Parentage and architectural particulars differ across the two accounts.
claims.boundary: Do not silently turn son of Simon and son of Onias into one agreed identification.
claims.nextQuestion: Record variant readings, authorial development and competing historical explanations.
claims.title: War 7.10.2-3 compared with Antiquities 13.3.1-3

claims.contribution: Lupus and Paulinus restrict the sanctuary; the transmitted duration is 343 years.
claims.boundary: No precise foundation or closure date is adopted from this inconsistent duration.
claims.nextQuestion: Investigate contacts before closure and possible dispersed institutions afterward.
claims.title: War 7.10.4

claims.contribution: Josephus describes a marrying Essene order concerned with succession.
claims.boundary: A wider household population does not establish the proposed demographic split or identify every community.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare household rules, actual names and institutional practice without a uniform celibate stereotype.
claims.title: War 2.8.13; compare CD 7:6-7 through Collins

claims.contribution: The passage identifies relations around a priestly murder involving Onias and Andronicus.
claims.boundary: The John-the-Baptist identification and a 20-year transition are additional claims.
claims.nextQuestion: Compare narrative sequence and historical carriers, not merely a shared execution motif.
claims.title: Second Maccabees 4:33-38

claims.contribution: Gruen proposes mutual support rather than a simply rival sanctuary model.
claims.boundary: Full-paper review and endorsement of the broader branch genealogy are not claimed.
claims.nextQuestion: Consult the full critical discussion and compare its argument with the actual Josephus passages.
claims.title: Published abstract, Scripta Classica Israelica 16 (1997), 47-70

references.title: Galatians 1, World English Bible
references.scope: Primary text: Paul's account of persecution, revelation, earlier apostles and a visit to Peter and James.

references.title: Galatians 2, World English Bible
references.scope: Primary text read in full, especially verses 1-10 on an interval, companions and recognized leaders. The passage does not by itself supply an absolute calendar date for the visit.

references.title: Gospel of Thomas, translation by Stephen Patterson and Marvin Meyer
references.scope: Translation consulted for sayings 1, 3, 12, 13, 39 and 108. The edition uses brief paraphrases and links, not a reproduction of the translation. Translation credit is distinct from an acknowledged influence in the author's older conversations.

references.title: Logan Williams (2023), Melchizedek, the Son of Man, and Eschatological Jubilee
references.scope: Full-text HTML consulted, particularly the author's translation of 11Q13 II 2-9 and discussion of II 6 and 13. His active-agent reading is distinguished from the critical edition he disputes. The critical edition itself has not been collated in this pass. This is current editorial research, not a recovered author acknowledgment.

references.title: Daniel 9, World English Bible
references.scope: Primary translated chapter consulted, especially verses 2, 15, 17 and 24-27. Exodus, sanctuary, desolation and restoration remain separate from any proposed absolute-year calculation.

references.title: Josephus, Antiquities 13.3.1-3, 13.10.4 and 13.13.2, Whiston translation
references.scope: Primary translated passages consulted for the sanctuary, royal petition and permission, Onias's sons Chelcias and Ananias, and Ananias's counsel concerning Alexander. Strabo is encountered through Josephus's quotation, not as an independently inspected document. These relations do not establish subsequent Teacher or Gnostic transmission.

references.title: John J. Collins, The Dead Sea Scrolls (Anchor Bible Dictionary, 1992)
references.scope: Sections C and J of the full online reproduction consulted for CD 1, CD 20:15, and household rules at CD 7:6-7. The 40-year Teacher career is a reconstructed interval. This is a dated scholarly interpretation, not a new Hebrew collation or current manuscript inventory.

references.title: Michal Jaroslaw Klukowski, The Tradition of the 364-Day Year in Second Temple Period Judaism
references.scope: Published scholarly abstract consulted for the 364-day schematic-year tradition and its relationship to calendrical texts. No claim of full-paper review, a settled origin, or a proved practical intercalation scheme is made.

references.title: Josephus, War 7.10.2-4, William Whiston translation
references.scope: Primary translated narrative consulted for the Onias sanctuary, different parentage and architectural description, support and closure under Lupus and Paulinus, and the transmitted 343-year duration. Editorial bracketed dates and Whiston notes are not words of the ancient narrative.

references.title: Josephus, War 2.8.13, William Whiston translation
references.scope: Primary translated passage consulted for the marrying Essene order and its concern with succession. It is not a roster of the households or branches proposed in this reconstruction.

references.title: Second Maccabees 4:33-38, USCCB translation
references.scope: Primary translated passage consulted for the death of Onias, the roles of Andronicus and Menelaus, and the king's response. It does not itself identify John the Baptist or a 20-year interval to the Teacher.

references.title: Erich S. Gruen, The Origins and Objectives of Onias' Temple (1997)
references.scope: Published abstract consulted. It challenges the conventional rival-temple account and proposes mutual support between Jerusalem and Leontopolis while noting problems in Josephus. The full article and its critical apparatus were not independently reviewed in this pass; publication is 1997, not the website upload date.

references.title: Eusebius, Church History 2.1 and 2.23, McGiffert translation
references.scope: Consulted the English translation of 2.1.3-4 and 2.23.4-18. Clement and Hegesippus are quoted through Eusebius, not independently recovered complete works. No Greek manuscript collation; narrative details are reported claims, not all independently established events.

references.title: Eusebius, Church History 3.27, McGiffert translation
references.scope: Consulted chapter 27 on the categories called Ebionites. An external polemical classification with internal distinctions, not an unmediated self-description or catalogue identification of an extant Hebrews gospel.

references.title: Eusebius, Church History 4.22, McGiffert translation
references.scope: Consulted 4.22.4-7, including Hegesippus on Symeon, the disputed succession and the classification of Essenes as opponents. The reported kinship and polemical framing remain explicit; no independent reconstruction of the lost Memoirs.

references.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 1.26.2, Roberts-Rambaut translation
references.scope: Consulted the translated Ebionite description, including Matthew, opposition to Paul, law observance and Creator affirmation. This is a hostile classifier, not a surviving membership statement from all groups given the name.

references.title: Josephus, Antiquities 20.200, Whiston translation
references.scope: Consulted the individual paragraph directly: James, the relational identification, and the Festus-Albinus interval. No new authenticity adjudication, identification of an interpolator, or independent calendar reconstruction is claimed.

references.title: Luke 11:52, World English Bible
references.scope: Primary translated passage for the criticism of obstructed access to knowledge. A thematic and functional comparison with Thomas 39, not a demonstrated direction of literary dependence.

references.title: First Apocalypse of James, William R. Schoedel translation
references.scope: Consulted the opening distinction between material and spiritual brotherhood through the indexed translation. Direct page retrieval was unavailable during this intake. This is not a full-text review or a new Greek/Coptic collation.

references.title: Simon Gathercole, A Proposed Rereading of P.Oxy. 654 line 41 (Gos. Thom. 7), 2006
references.scope: Consulted the Cambridge-published extract describing the partial Greek Thomas witnesses P.Oxy. 1 and P.Oxy. 655. The full article and proposed line-41 rereading were not reviewed; its witness description does not date the complete Coptic collection.

references.title: University of Texas, Smith and Landau report Greek First Apocalypse of James fragments, 2017
references.scope: Institutional report of the researchers' discovery, published November 29, 2017. Fifth/sixth-century dating and possible educational use are reported interpretations. The later critical edition and physical fragments were not independently inspected. The report assigns fragment and image rights to the Egypt Exploration Society.

references.title: Lance S. Owens, The Gospel of Thomas and the Hermeneutics of Vision, 2002
references.scope: Earlier interpretive essay, copyright 2002, consulted through indexed text. Credits the James/apocalyptic/transformative-reading comparison without adopting all historical assertions or claiming a demonstrated chain to Kabbalah. This is a newly consulted comparison, not a documented personal influence on the older conversations.
